_comment: Jurisdiction config (docs/uplift/migration/04-jurisdiction.md Steps 1-2). primary_instruments is the WA statutory framework this council is actually assessed against — the future framework_refs claim-object field (02-claim-layer.md) will resolve {instrument, section} pairs against this table. secondary_mapping is Nolan/CIPFA, demoted here (not deleted) since it's a real, recognised governance standard, just not the primary jurisdiction one for a WA council. config/test_registry.json's own `principles` field remains the single source of truth for which citation each battery test actually states (docs/uplift/migration/04-jurisdiction.md Step 1) — this file does not duplicate that per-test mapping, only the underlying instrument/principle definitions.

LGA_1995.name: Local Government Act 1995 (WA)
LGA_1995.relevance: The primary statute — general conduct obligations, financial interest disclosure (s5.65), council-resolution exceptions (s5.68), meeting procedure.

ADMIN_REGS.name: Local Government (Administration) Regulations 1996 (WA)
ADMIN_REGS.relevance: Meeting procedure, minute-keeping, and administrative detail under the Act.

FG_REGS.name: Local Government (Functions and General) Regulations 1996 (WA)
FG_REGS.relevance: Tendering, procurement thresholds, and delegation detail — the WA analogue of a procurement-integrity framework.

CONDUCT_REGS.name: Local Government (Rules of Conduct) Regulations 2007 (WA)
CONDUCT_REGS.relevance: The conduct-standard instrument in force for the pre-2021 era of this corpus; superseded in scope by MODEL_CODE_2021, not repealed retroactively — era-boundary relevant (see config/council_eras.json's conduct_regs_2007 key).

MODEL_CODE_2021.name: Local Government (Model Code of Conduct) Regulations 2021 (WA)
MODEL_CODE_2021.relevance: The current conduct-standard instrument — era-boundary relevant (see config/council_eras.json's model_code_2021 key).

DLGSC.name: Department of Local Government, Sport and Cultural Industries (WA)
DLGSC.relevance: Interpretive guidance issuer, not a binding instrument itself — cited for how a provision is expected to be applied, not as the legal basis.

SAT.name: State Administrative Tribunal (WA)
SAT.relevance: Precedent body — decisions here are persuasive on how a provision (e.g. reg 34C on delegate declarations) has actually been read, not binding statute.

secondary_mapping._comment: Demoted, not deleted (docs/uplift/migration/04-jurisdiction.md G-01) — a real, widely-recognised governance standard (UK CSPL / CIPFA-SOLACE), just not the primary jurisdiction one for a WA council. Definitions verbatim from docs/investigator/Investigator_prompt.txt Parts 1.1/1.2 — the same source frontend/src/components/Glossary.tsx's tooltip dictionary uses, kept in sync by hand across the two runtimes (Python config vs. frontend TS), not by a shared loader.

nolan.selflessness: Decisions solely in the public interest, not for self, family, or friends.
nolan.integrity: No obligations to outsiders who might influence you.
nolan.accountability: Submit to whatever scrutiny is appropriate.
nolan.openness: Act and decide transparently; restrict information only with good reason.
nolan.leadership: Model these principles and challenge breaches in others.

cipfa.A: Integrity, ethical values, rule of law — codes of conduct, interest declarations, whistleblowing arrangements.
cipfa.C: Defining outcomes in terms of sustainable economic/social/environmental benefits.
cipfa.D: Determining the interventions to achieve those outcomes (incl. value for money).
cipfa.E: Developing capacity — of the entity and of its leadership.
cipfa.F: Managing risks and performance through robust internal control and strong public financial management.
cipfa.G: Transparency, reporting and audit to deliver accountability.
